explain.title: Common factors
explain.body: In algebra, a common factor is an expression that divides two or more expressions exactly. For example, 2x − 6 = 2(x − 3), so 2 is a common factor of both terms.

explain.title: Trinomials and binomials
explain.body: Trinomial factoring is converting trinomial expression as a product of two binomial expressions. A trinomial is an expression with three terms and binomial is an expression with two terms.

explain.title: Factor quadratics by grouping
explain.body: For x² + px + q, find two numbers whose product is q and whose sum is p. For ax² + bx + c, multiply a by c, find a factor pair with the required sum, split the middle term, and group.

explain.title: Use identities for quartics and cubes
explain.body: A quartic expression may be rewritten as a difference of squares. For cubes, use a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) or a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).

mistakes: Taking out a factor that is not common to every term, or not taking out the highest common factor.
Choosing two numbers whose sum is right but whose product is wrong when splitting a middle term.
Forgetting to factor the common binomial after grouping.
Using the wrong signs in the sum or difference of cubes identity.
Assuming (a + b)² = a² + b² or (a + b)³ = a³ + b³.

explain.title: Highest Common Factor
explain.body: The HCF of two or more algebraic expressions refers to the greatest algebraic expression which divides them without leaving a remainder. Factor each expression, then multiply only the factors shared by all of them.

explain.title: HCF by division
explain.body: Divide the polynomial with the higher degree by the other polynomial. If there is a remainder, continue using the divisor and remainder. A constant factor that is not common to all the given polynomials is ignored, as shown in your textbook.

explain.title: Least Common Multiple
explain.body: The LCM of two or more algebraic expressions is the smallest expression that is divisible by each of the given expressions. By factorization, use the factors required by the expressions, taking each factor at its greatest required power.

explain.title: Relationship between LCM and HCF
explain.body: For two polynomials, LCM × HCF = p(x) × q(x). To find a missing polynomial, divide LCM × HCF by the polynomial already given. To find the product, multiply the LCM by the HCF.

mistakes: For the HCF, including a factor that is not common to every expression.
For the LCM, leaving out a factor or using a lower power than is required.
Confusing the HCF and LCM rules: HCF uses common factors, while the LCM includes all required factors.
Forgetting to factor completely before identifying common or required factors.
Using LCM × HCF = p(x) × q(x) incorrectly; write the relationship first and substitute carefully.
Leaving out the zero remainder when showing division proves that one polynomial divides another.

explain.title: What a square root means
explain.body: The square root of an algebraic expression refers to a value that, when multiplied by itself, gives the original expression. Just like finding the square root of a number, taking the square root of an algebraic expression involves determining what expression, when squared, results in the given expression.

explain.title: Factorization method
explain.body: Rewrite the polynomial as a perfect square, such as (x − 4)². Then take the square root of the square factor and follow your textbook's sign notation.

explain.title: Division method
explain.body: When the degree of the polynomial is higher, division method in finding the square root is very useful. Start with the square root of the leading term, double the root found so far to obtain the next term, and continue until the remainder is zero.

explain.title: Using factors in applications
explain.body: For a question asking when a function is zero, factorize the expression and set each variable factor equal to zero. Then state the values of x.

mistakes: Forgetting the negative sign in the middle term when recognising a square such as (x − 4)².
In the division method, forgetting to double the root found so far before finding the next quotient term.
Stopping before checking that the remainder is zero.
Leaving out one of the zero values after factorizing an expression.
Changing the signs or final form given in your textbook's answer key.

notes.title: How to factorize algebraic expressions
notes.answer: Factor out common factors first; if there are none, use the method that matches the expression.
notes.explanation: A common factor is taken outside brackets. For a trinomial, split the middle term into two terms whose product and sum fit the expression, then group terms. For example, x² + 9x + 14 = (x + 2)(x + 7). For cubes, use the identities for a³ + b³ or a³ − b³.
notes.simple: Factorization means rewriting an expression as a product of simpler expressions. Look for a common factor first; otherwise, use the suitable factorization method.
steps: Look for a factor common to every term and take it outside brackets.
For x² + px + q, find two numbers whose product is q and whose sum is p.
For ax² + bx + c, multiply a by c, split the middle term, then group.
For a⁴-type expressions, make a difference of squares when possible.
For cubes, identify the cube terms and use the sum or difference of cubes identity.

notes.title: Finding HCF and LCM of Algebraic Expressions
notes.answer: The HCF is the greatest common factor; the LCM is the smallest expression divisible by all the given expressions.
notes.explanation: To find an HCF, identify the greatest expression that divides every given expression without a remainder. To find an LCM, include every factor needed to make an expression divisible by each given expression. For two polynomials, use LCM × HCF = product of the polynomials.
notes.simple: HCF means the biggest factor shared by all the expressions. LCM means the smallest expression that contains all the factors needed by each one.
examples: For 6x²y and 9xy², the common factors are 3, x and y, so the HCF is 3xy.
For x² − 1 and x² + x, factor them as (x − 1)(x + 1) and x(x + 1). The LCM is x(x − 1)(x + 1).
steps: For the HCF, multiply only the factors common to every expression, using the smallest power of each.
For the LCM, include each factor that occurs, using its greatest power.
For two polynomials, use LCM × HCF = product of the two polynomials to find a missing polynomial or their product.
notes.checkQuestion: What is the HCF of x² − 1 and x² + x?

notes.title: Finding the square root of a polynomial
notes.answer: The square root of a perfect-square polynomial is the expression whose square equals that polynomial.
notes.explanation: A square root is an expression that gives the original expression when multiplied by itself. For a perfect-square polynomial, factor it as a square or use the division method, then write the square root with the sign shown in your textbook.
notes.simple: Find the expression that, when squared, gives the polynomial. For example, (x − 4)² gives x² − 8x + 16.
examples: x² − 8x + 16 = (x − 4)², so its square root is ±(x − 4).
x⁴ − 12x³ + 42x² − 36x + 9 = (x² − 6x + 3)², so its square root is ±(x² − 6x + 3).
steps: For the factorization method, rewrite the polynomial as a perfect square.
For the division method, find the first square-root term from the first term of the polynomial.
Double the root found so far, use it to find the next term, and continue until the remainder is zero.
Take the square root and include the sign or signs used in your textbook.
notes.checkQuestion: What is the square root of x² − 6x + 9?

steps: Look for a common factor and take it out.

For HCF and LCM, factor each polynomial first.

rationales: This is correct because it expands to x³ + 3x² + 3x + 1.
This is incorrect because it expands to x³ − 3x² + 3x − 1.
This is incorrect because it expands to x³ + 2x² + 2x + 1.
This is incorrect because it expands to x³ − 1.

quiz.stem: Cubic polynomial has degree:
rationales: This is incorrect because degree 1 is linear.
This is incorrect because degree 2 is quadratic.
This is correct because a cubic polynomial has degree 3.
This is incorrect because degree 4 is quartic.

quiz.stem: One of the factors of x³ − 27 is:
rationales: This is correct because x³ − 27 = (x − 3)(x² + 3x + 9).
This is incorrect because x + 3 is not a factor of x³ − 27.
This is incorrect because the quadratic factor has a positive, not negative, middle term.
This is incorrect because option c is not a factor, so both a and c cannot be correct.

written.text: Factorize by identifying common factors: 15y² + 20y

rubric.description: Identify and take out the common factor 5y.
rubric.why: Taking out the highest common factor is the key step.
rubric.how: Write 15y² + 20y = 5y(3y + 4).

rubric.why: The final factors must multiply back to the original expression.
rubric.how: Finish with 5y(3y + 4).

written.text: Factorize: x² + 4x + 3

rubric.description: Split and group the middle term.
rubric.why: Splitting the middle term shows the product-and-sum method.
rubric.how: Use 1 and 3, whose product is 3 and sum is 4.

rubric.why: The final factors must multiply back to the given trinomial.
rubric.how: Take the common binomial factor from the grouped terms.

written.text: Factorize: x² + x − 12

rubric.description: Split the middle term and group.
rubric.why: The middle term must be split using numbers with product −12 and sum 1.
rubric.how: Use 4 and −3, then factor each group.

rubric.why: The final factors must reproduce all three terms.
rubric.how: Take out the common binomial factor.

written.text: Factorize: 6 + 7x − 3x²

rubric.description: Rearrange and split the middle term.
rubric.why: A suitable split of the middle term makes grouping possible.
rubric.how: Write the expression as 6 + 9x − 2x − 3x².

rubric.why: Both groups must contain the same binomial factor.
rubric.how: Take out 3 from the first group and −x from the second.

rubric.why: The answer must be a correct factorization of the original expression.
rubric.how: Reorder the binomial terms to match the answer key.

written.text: Factorize: x⁴ + 4x² + 16

rubric.description: Rewrite as a difference of squares.
rubric.why: Adding and subtracting a suitable term creates a difference of squares.
rubric.how: Use (x² + 4)² − (2x)².

rubric.why: The difference of squares must be factored with both signs.
rubric.how: Take A = x² + 4 and B = 2x.

rubric.why: The final answer must have the factors correctly simplified.
rubric.how: Write the two quadratic factors.

written.text: Factorize: x⁴ − 14x² + 1

rubric.why: The expression is rewritten as a difference of squares.
rubric.how: Use (x² + 1)² − (4x)².

rubric.description: Apply the difference of squares identity.
rubric.why: Both conjugate factors are needed to preserve the expression.
rubric.how: Factor A² − B² as (A − B)(A + B).

rubric.why: The final factors must match the given expression.
rubric.how: Arrange each factor in descending powers.

written.text: Factorize: (3x² + 5x + 3)(3x² + 5x + 5) − 3

rubric.description: Set the common expression equal to y.
rubric.why: The repeated quadratic expression is replaced by one variable to simplify the work.
rubric.how: Let y = 3x² + 5x.

rubric.description: Expand and factorize the expression in y.
rubric.why: Expanding produces a trinomial that can be factorized by grouping.
rubric.how: Obtain y² + 8y + 12, then split 8y as 6y + 2y.

rubric.why: This is the factorization of the trinomial in the temporary variable.
rubric.how: Group the terms and take out the common binomial.

rubric.why: Substituting back gives the required expression in x.
rubric.how: Replace y with 3x² + 5x.

written.text: Factorize: (x + 1)(x − 1)(x + 2)(x − 2) − 16x²

rubric.why: Pairing conjugate factors uses the difference of squares and simplifies the expression.
This rewriting creates a difference of squares.
rubric.how: Express it as (x² + 2)² − (5x)².

rubric.description: Apply the difference of squares identity.
rubric.why: Factoring both signs correctly gives the two quadratic factors.
rubric.how: Use (A − B)(A + B).

rubric.why: The final answer must be the required factorization.
rubric.how: Arrange the terms in each factor.

written.text: Factorize: 8x³ + 12x² + 6x + 1

rubric.description: Match the expression to the cube pattern.
rubric.why: Recognising the terms as a binomial cube identifies the correct identity.
rubric.how: Recognise a = 2x and b = 1.

rubric.description: Apply the sum-of-cubes pattern for a perfect cube.
rubric.why: The binomial cube is the factorization of the given four-term expression.
rubric.how: Write the expression as (2x + 1)³.

rubric.why: The answer must state the complete factorization.
rubric.how: Write the cube or its three equal factors.

written.text: Factorize: 64x³ + 125

rubric.why: Identifying the two cubes gives the values needed for the identity.
rubric.how: Write 64x³ + 125 = (4x)³ + 5³.

rubric.description: Apply the sum of cubes identity.
rubric.why: The sum of cubes uses a plus in the first factor and a minus middle term in the second.
rubric.how: Use a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²).

rubric.why: The factors must be correctly simplified and complete.
rubric.how: Simplify each term in the quadratic factor.

written.text: Factorize: 27 − 512y³

rubric.why: Recognising the difference of cubes identifies the correct identity.
rubric.how: Write 27 − 512y³ = 3³ − (8y)³.

rubric.description: Apply the difference of cubes identity.
rubric.why: The difference of cubes has a minus in the first factor and plus signs in the quadratic factor.
rubric.how: Use a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).

rubric.why: The final factors must be simplified correctly.
rubric.how: Evaluate the squares and product in the second factor.

written.text: Find HCF by factorization method: 21x²y, 35xy²

rubric.description: Identify the common numerical and variable factors.
rubric.why: Writing the expressions as factors shows which factors are shared.
rubric.how: Factor the numerical coefficients and the variables in both expressions.

rubric.why: The final HCF must include exactly the common factors.
rubric.how: Multiply the common factors 7, x and y.

written.text: Find HCF by factorization method: 4x² − 9y², 2x² − 3xy

rubric.why: Correctly factoring the difference of squares reveals its factors.
rubric.how: Use the difference of two squares.

rubric.why: Factoring the second expression reveals its common binomial factor.
rubric.how: Take x as the common factor.

rubric.why: The HCF is the factor shared by both factorizations.
rubric.how: Identify the common factor and give it as the final answer.

written.text: Find HCF by factorization method: a³ + 2a² − 3a, 2a³ + 5a² − 3a

rubric.why: The first complete factorization makes its possible common factors visible.
rubric.how: Take out a and factor the remaining quadratic.

rubric.why: The second complete factorization confirms the shared factors.
rubric.how: Take out a and factor the remaining quadratic.

rubric.why: The final HCF contains the factors common to both expressions.
rubric.how: Multiply the common factors a and a + 3.

written.text: Find HCF by factorization method: x² + 15x + 56, x² + 5x − 24, x² + 8x

rubric.why: Factoring the first expression identifies its factors.
rubric.how: Find two numbers with product 56 and sum 15.

rubric.why: Factoring the second expression shows the shared factor.
rubric.how: Find two numbers with product −24 and sum 5.

rubric.why: Factoring the third expression confirms the common binomial.
rubric.how: Take x as the common factor.

rubric.why: The final answer is the factor common to all three expressions.
rubric.how: Give the shared factor.

written.text: Find HCF of the following expressions by using division method: 27x³ + 9x² − 3x − 10, 3x − 2

rubric.why: A zero remainder shows that the divisor divides the polynomial exactly.
rubric.how: Divide the cubic polynomial by 3x − 2 and obtain quotient 9x² + 9x + 5.

rubric.why: The exact divisor is the HCF for this pair.
rubric.how: Give the divisor after confirming the remainder is zero.

written.text: Find HCF of the following expressions by using division method: x³ − 9x² + 23x − 15, x² − 4x + 3

rubric.description: Divide the cubic polynomial by the quadratic.
rubric.why: The quotient and zero remainder show the first polynomial is divisible by the second.
rubric.how: Obtain quotient x − 5 with remainder zero.

rubric.why: A zero remainder establishes exact divisibility.
rubric.how: Show that the division has no remainder.

rubric.why: The divisor is the HCF once it divides the other expression exactly.
rubric.how: Give the quadratic divisor as the final answer.

written.text: Find LCM of the following expressions by using prime factorization method: 2a²b, 4ab², 6ab

rubric.description: Identify the required numerical and variable factors.
rubric.why: Prime factorization identifies the greatest powers needed for the LCM.
rubric.how: Take the least common multiple of 2, 4 and 6, and the greatest powers a² and b².

rubric.why: The LCM must include every required factor.
rubric.how: Multiply the selected factors.

written.text: Find LCM of the following expressions by using prime factorization method: a² − 4a + 4, a² − 2a

rubric.why: Factoring the first expression reveals its repeated factor.
rubric.how: Recognize the perfect-square trinomial.

rubric.why: Factoring the second expression reveals its factors.
rubric.how: Take out the common factor a.

rubric.why: The LCM uses each factor at its greatest required power.
rubric.how: Include a and the greater power, (a − 2)².

rubric.why: The final expression is divisible by both given expressions.
rubric.how: Multiply the selected factors.

written.text: Find LCM of the following expressions by using prime factorization method: x⁴ − 16, x³ − 4x

rubric.why: Factoring the first expression reveals its factors.
rubric.how: Use the difference of two squares.

rubric.why: Factoring the second expression identifies its additional factor x.
rubric.how: Take out x and factor x² − 4.

rubric.description: Select the factors for the LCM.
rubric.why: The LCM includes each distinct factor required by the two expressions.
rubric.how: Include x, x − 2, x + 2 and x² + 4.

rubric.why: The final expression is divisible by both given expressions.
rubric.how: Write the product of the required factors, or its equivalent form.

written.text: Find LCM of the following expressions by using prime factorization method: 16 − 4x², x² + x − 6, 4 − x²

rubric.why: The first expression factors into 4 and the shared difference of squares.
rubric.how: Factor out 4.

rubric.why: Factoring the trinomial reveals a factor shared with 4 − x².
rubric.how: Find two numbers with product −6 and sum 1.

rubric.why: Factoring the third expression confirms the factors already included.
rubric.how: Use the difference of two squares.

rubric.why: The final LCM includes all factors at their required powers.
rubric.how: Combine the required factors and give the equivalent book answer.

written.text: The HCF of two polynomials is y − 7 and their LCM is y³ − 10y² + 11y + 70. If one of the polynomials is y² − 5y − 14, find the other.

rubric.why: The relationship between LCM, HCF and the two polynomials sets up the calculation.
rubric.how: Write the other polynomial as (LCM × HCF) divided by the given polynomial.

rubric.why: Factoring the given polynomial makes cancellation possible.
rubric.how: Factor y² − 5y − 14.

rubric.description: Divide and state the other polynomial.
rubric.why: The quotient gives the missing polynomial.
rubric.how: Simplify the relationship and give the quotient.

written.text: The LCM and HCF of two polynomial p(x) and q(x) are 36x³(x + a)(x³ − a³) and x²(x − a) respectively. If p(x) = 4x²(x² − a²), find q(x).

rubric.why: The relationship gives an expression for the unknown polynomial.
rubric.how: Use q(x) = (LCM × HCF)/p(x).

rubric.description: Substitute the given LCM, HCF and p(x).
rubric.why: Substituting all the given expressions is needed for correct simplification.
rubric.how: Place the product of LCM and HCF over p(x).

rubric.why: Factoring the difference of squares allows common factors to cancel.
rubric.how: Use x² − a² = (x − a)(x + a) and cancel common factors.

rubric.why: The simplified expression is the required second polynomial.
rubric.how: Give the remaining expression after cancellation.

written.text: The HCF and LCM of two polynomials is (x + a) and 12x²(x + a)(x² − a²) respectively. Find the product of the two polynomials.
modelAnswer: Product of the two polynomials = LCM × HCF

rubric.why: The product of two polynomials equals their LCM multiplied by their HCF.
rubric.how: Write product = LCM × HCF.

rubric.why: Correct substitution keeps all given factors in the product.
rubric.how: Multiply the stated LCM by the stated HCF.

rubric.why: Factoring the difference of squares allows the product to be written in factorized form.
rubric.how: Use x² − a² = (x − a)(x + a).

rubric.why: The final answer correctly combines all factors and powers.
rubric.how: Combine the factors and give the simplified result.

written.text: Find the square root by factorization method: x² − 8x + 16
written.followUp: Find the square root of the following polynomials by factorization method: (i) x² − 8x + 16

rubric.description: Factor the polynomial as a square.
rubric.why: Recognising the perfect-square trinomial is the key factorization step.
rubric.how: Show x² − 8x + 16 = (x − 4)².

rubric.why: The final square-root expression is required for the answer.
rubric.how: Write ±(x − 4), as in your textbook.

written.text: Find the square root by factorization method: 36a² + 84a + 49
written.followUp: Find the square root of the following polynomials by factorization method: (i) x² − 8x + 16

rubric.why: The perfect-square factorization shows how to take the root.
The square-root expression completes the answer.
rubric.how: Write ±(6a + 7).

written.text: Find the square root by factorization method: 64y² − 32y + 4
written.followUp: Find the square root of the following polynomials by factorization method: (i) x² − 8x + 16

rubric.why: Factoring as a square is the essential method step.
The final square root earns the remaining mark.
rubric.how: Write ±(8y − 2).

written.text: Find the square root by factorization method: 200t² − 120t + 18
written.followUp: Find the square root of the following polynomials by factorization method: (i) x² − 8x + 16

rubric.why: Taking out the common factor reveals the perfect square.
The square root of the remaining factor must be included.

written.text: Find the square root by factorization method: 40x² + 120x + 90
written.followUp: Find the square root of the following polynomials by factorization method: (i) x² − 8x + 16

rubric.why: Taking out the common factor displays the square trinomial.
The final answer must include the square root of 10.

written.text: Find the square root by division method: 4x⁴ − 28x³ + 37x² + 42x + 9
modelAnswer: Double 2x² to get 4x²; dividing −28x³ by 4x² gives −7x
Double (2x² − 7x) to get 4x² − 14x; dividing −12x² by 4x² gives −3
written.followUp: Find the square root of the following polynomials by factorization method: (i) x² − 8x + 16

rubric.why: The first root term comes from the first term of the polynomial.
rubric.how: Use √(4x⁴) = 2x².

rubric.why: The doubled partial root is used to find the next term.
rubric.how: Double 2x² to get 4x², then divide −28x³ by 4x² to get −7x.

rubric.why: The final quotient term must make the remainder zero.
rubric.how: The next term is −3 and the remainder is zero.

rubric.why: The complete square-root expression is the requested result.
rubric.how: Write ±(2x² − 7x − 3).

written.text: Find the square root by division method: 121x⁴ − 198x³ − 183x² + 216x + 144
modelAnswer: Double 11x² to get 22x²; dividing −198x³ by 22x² gives −9x
Double (11x² − 9x) to get 22x² − 18x; dividing −264x² by 22x² gives −12
written.followUp: Find the square root of the following polynomials by factorization method: (i) x² − 8x + 16

rubric.why: The leading term of the square root comes from the leading polynomial term.
rubric.how: Use √(121x⁴) = 11x².

rubric.why: Doubling the partial root gives the divisor used to find the next term.
rubric.how: Double 11x² to get 22x², then divide −198x³ by 22x².

rubric.why: The last term completes the square-root division with zero remainder.
rubric.how: The remaining quotient term is −12 and the remainder is zero.

rubric.why: The answer must state the complete square root.
rubric.how: Write ±(11x² − 9x − 12).

written.text: Factorize the expression and find the investment levels that result in zero return: R(x) = −x² + 6x − 8
modelAnswer: For zero return, x − 2 = 0 or x − 4 = 0
written.followUp: Find the square root of the following polynomials by factorization method: (i) x² − 8x + 16

rubric.why: The factorized expression makes the zero-return values visible.
Setting each factor to zero gives both investment levels.
rubric.how: State x = 2 or x = 4.

written.text: Find the break-even point(s), where the profit is zero: P(x) = x³ − 15x² + 75x − 125
written.followUp: Find the square root of the following polynomials by factorization method: (i) x² − 8x + 16

rubric.why: Recognising the cubic perfect power identifies the factor giving zero profit.
rubric.how: Show P(x) = (x − 5)³.

rubric.why: Solving the factor equal to zero gives the break-even point.
rubric.how: Set x − 5 = 0 and write x = 5.

written.text: Determine where the potential energy is zero: V(x) = 2x³ − 6x² + 4x
modelAnswer: For zero potential energy, x = 0 or x − 1 = 0 or x − 2 = 0
written.followUp: Find the square root of the following polynomials by factorization method: (i) x² − 8x + 16

rubric.why: Factorizing gives the factors whose zero values make the expression zero.
rubric.how: Show V(x) = 2x(x − 1)(x − 2).

rubric.why: Each variable factor gives a value where the potential energy is zero.
rubric.how: Write x = 0, x = 1 or x = 2.

written.text: Find the points of zero deflection: Y(x) = 2x² − 8x + 6
modelAnswer: For zero deflection, x − 1 = 0 or x − 3 = 0
written.followUp: Find the square root of the following polynomials by factorization method: (i) x² − 8x + 16

rubric.why: The factorization shows which values make the deflection zero.
Both factor equations must be solved to find all zero-deflection points.
rubric.how: Write x = 1 or x = 3.

written.text: Factorize the following expressions: 4x³ + 18x² − 12x

rubric.why: Taking out the common factor is the essential first step.
rubric.how: Identify and factor out 2x.

rubric.why: The final product must expand to the original expression.
rubric.how: Write the quotient inside the brackets.

written.text: Factorize the following expressions: x³ + 64y³

rubric.why: Recognizing the sum of cubes gives the first factor.
rubric.how: Use x³ + (4y)³.

rubric.why: The complete identity is needed to factor the expression correctly.
rubric.how: Apply a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²).

written.text: Factorize the following expressions: x³y³ − 8

rubric.why: Recognizing the difference of cubes gives the first factor.
rubric.how: Write the expression as (xy)³ − 2³.

rubric.why: The complete identity gives the correct factorization.
rubric.how: Apply a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).

written.text: Factorize the following expressions: −x² − 23x − 60

rubric.why: Taking out the negative sign makes the quadratic easier to factor.
rubric.how: Rewrite the expression as −(x² + 23x + 60).

rubric.description: Factor the quadratic and state the answer.
rubric.why: The two binomial factors must multiply to the expression inside the negative sign.
rubric.how: Find two numbers with product 60 and sum 23.

written.text: Factorize the following expressions: 2x² + 7x + 3

rubric.description: Find suitable factors for the quadratic.
rubric.why: Choosing factors that give the middle term is the key factorization step.
rubric.how: Split the middle term or check the product and sum.

rubric.why: The final factors must multiply to the given trinomial.
rubric.how: Write the two binomial factors.

written.text: Factorize the following expressions: x⁴ + 64

rubric.why: Rewriting the expression as a difference of squares reveals a factorization.
rubric.how: Use (x² + 8)² − (4x)².

rubric.why: The difference-of-squares identity supplies the two factors.
rubric.how: Factor as (x² + 8 + 4x)(x² + 8 − 4x).

rubric.why: The final factors must be correct and equivalent to the original expression.
rubric.how: Arrange each factor in standard order and give the final result.

written.text: Factorize the following expressions: x⁴ + 2x² + 9

rubric.description: Rewrite as a difference of squares.
rubric.why: This rewriting makes the expression a difference of squares.
rubric.how: Use (x² + 3)² − (2x)².

rubric.why: The identity gives the two factors before arranging terms.
rubric.how: Factor (x² + 3)² − (2x)².

rubric.why: The correct final factors show the expression has been factorized fully.
rubric.how: Arrange the two factors in standard order.

written.text: Factorize the following expressions: (x² + 6x + 3)(x² + 6x − 9) + 36

rubric.why: Using a shared expression makes the factors easier to see.
rubric.how: Let the common part be x² + 6x − 3.

rubric.why: This correctly rewrites the two brackets in terms of the common expression.
rubric.how: Express them as the common part plus 6 and minus 6.

rubric.description: Simplify and state the final answer.
rubric.why: The simplification must lead to the exact square shown in the answer key.

written.text: Find LCM and HCF: 4x³ + 12x², 8x² + 16x

rubric.why: Factoring both expressions is needed before finding their HCF and LCM.
rubric.how: Take out the common numerical and variable factors.

rubric.why: The HCF uses the common factors at their lowest powers.
rubric.how: Take the common factors from the two factorizations.

rubric.why: The LCM must contain every factor at its highest power.
rubric.how: Take each factor at its highest power.

written.text: Find LCM and HCF: x³ + 3x² − 4x, x² − 4x + 3

rubric.why: Both polynomials must be factored before the common factors can be compared.
rubric.how: Factor the cubic and the quadratic fully.

rubric.why: The HCF is the factor common to both expressions.
rubric.how: Identify the shared factor.

rubric.why: The LCM must include all factors at their greatest powers.
rubric.how: Combine all distinct factors from the two factorizations.

written.text: Find LCM and HCF: x² + 8x + 16, x² − 16

rubric.why: The factors reveal the common factor and the highest powers needed.
rubric.how: Use a perfect-square trinomial and a difference of squares.

rubric.why: The HCF is the common factor with the lowest power.
rubric.how: Identify the factor present in both expressions.

rubric.why: The LCM uses each factor at its highest power.
rubric.how: Use the greatest power of each distinct factor.

written.text: Find LCM and HCF: x³ − 9x, x² − x − 6

rubric.why: Factoring both polynomials shows all factors needed for the HCF and LCM.
rubric.how: Factor out x in the first, then factor the quadratics.

rubric.why: The HCF is the shared factor.
rubric.how: Identify the factor common to both expressions.

rubric.why: The LCM must include every factor at its highest power.
rubric.how: Combine the distinct factors without leaving out x.

written.text: Find square root by factorization and division method of the expression 16x⁴ + 8x² + 1.

rubric.description: Factor the expression as a perfect square.
rubric.why: Recognizing the perfect-square trinomial gives its square root.
rubric.how: Match the first and last terms and the middle term.

rubric.why: Both positive and negative expressions have the same square.
rubric.how: Include the ± sign in the final answer.
